text:
ana: heads up — after installing redwoodctl 0.10.1 via winget on a fresh Win11 box, the `redwoodctl` command isn't recognized until I open a new cmd. installer claims it added to PATH though. anyone seen this with winget?

kevin: i've seen similar when the installer updates user PATH but the current shell doesn't pick it up. did you install for CurrentUser vs AllUsers? winget defaults to CurrentUser iirc.

ana: installed with `winget install Redwood.Inference.redwoodctl` (no elevation). PATH shows `C:\Users\ana\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps` contains a shim. `where redwoodctl` returns that path but cmd still says 'not recognized'.

lee: weird, WindowsApps shims can be flaky. try `refreshenv` if you have chocolatey, or run `exec $env:PATH = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PATH','User') + ';' + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PATH','Machine')` in pwsh to reload.

ana: ok reload fixed it in pwsh. but another thing: `redwoodctl auth login --profile staging` says login successful but `redwoodctl config current` still shows `default`. i expected login to switch active profile.

kevin: that's historically been ambiguous. `auth login` writes creds to the credentials file but doesn't change the active profile unless you pass `--set-current` or run `config set-current`. docs might be unclear.

ana: ah there is a `--set-current`? not in `redwoodctl auth login --help` output for 0.10.1.

cli-bot: Tip: `redwoodctl auth login --help` output (0.10.1):
```
Usage: redwoodctl auth login [OPTIONS]
  Log in to Redwood and store credentials for a profile.
Options:
  --profile <name>  Profile name to save credentials under.
  --org <org>       Organization to log into.
  --help            Show help.
```
No `--set-current` flag present.

lee: ok so bug: auth login docs mention optionally making profile active but flag isn't implemented. please open issue. also for local testing `redwoodctl serve --local` seems to read active profile from `REDWOOD_PROFILE` env var first, then from `~/.redwoodctl/config.json`. we should be consistent.

ana: filed issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/1462 titled "auth login missing --set-current; inconsistent profile precedence for local serve" with repro and notes.

kevin: workaround: `redwoodctl config set-current staging` or `setx REDWOOD_PROFILE staging` for system-wide. `setx` requires new shell though.

ana: also ran into an auth edge while testing sample app: when `redwoodctl run sample-app` spawns a local dev server it uses the default profile even though `REDWOOD_PROFILE` set in my GitHub Codespaces environment. not sure if the child process is inheriting env vars there.

lee: child processes should inherit, but Codespaces uses a wrapper. maybe `run` drops env for sandboxing. can you run with `REDWOOD_PROFILE=staging redwoodctl run sample-app --debug` and paste logs?

ana: log excerpt: `DEBUG: env REDWOOD_PROFILE=staging` then later `INFO: using profile=default (no active profile set)`

kevin: looks like code path checks env early, but later the config loader overwrites with config.json default. race/ordering bug. i'll add a unit test to ensure env takes precedence.

lee: small DX nit — on Windows the installer doesn't offer to add completion to Powershell profile. would be nice `redwoodctl completion --install` to try to append and tell users if execution policy blocks it.

cli-bot: Feature request logged in the issue: add `--install` for completions + check PowerShell execution policy.

ana: one more: `redwoodctl version` shows `0.10.1 (built 2026-02-02)` which is great for triage. please keep build metadata.

kevin: agreed. impl note: auth login should probably write token then update in-memory active profile so immediate `whoami` reflects change. low-risk change. i'll draft a patch.

devex-bot: @devex FYI issue #1462 created and linked to milestone v0.10.2.

ana: thanks all — workarounds ok for now. will test patch when it's up. :+1:
